hints: List the SI base quantities, then remove the three quantities already named in the question.
The remaining accepted choices are time, electric current, amount of substance and luminous intensity; select any two.
walkthrough: The seven SI base quantities are length, mass, time, electric current, thermodynamic temperature, amount of substance and luminous intensity.
Length, mass and temperature have already been given in the question.
The remaining choices are time, electric current, amount of substance and luminous intensity.
Any two different choices from those four earn the two available marks.

ai_rubric.observable: States any two different SI base quantities from time, electric current, amount of substance and luminous intensity.

hints: Use the pendulum equation exactly as supplied, with the measured length in metres and the period in seconds.
Square the period before dividing 4π² times the length by that result.
walkthrough: The supplied relation gives g = 4π²l / T².
Substitute l = 1.50 m and T = 2.48 s: g = (4π² × 1.50) / (2.48)².
Evaluating the expression gives g = 9.63 m s⁻².

ai_rubric.observable: Correctly evaluates the supplied pendulum relation to obtain 9.63 m s⁻² for g.

hints: For a product or quotient, add percentage uncertainties; first note how the period appears in the supplied equation.
The length contributes 2%, while the period is squared and so contributes twice 3%.
walkthrough: In g = 4π²l / T², the constant 4π² has no uncertainty contribution.
The length l contributes its 2% uncertainty.
Because T is squared, its 3% uncertainty is doubled to 6%.
Add the contributions: percentage uncertainty in g = 2% + 6% = 8%.

ai_rubric.observable: Adds 2% from the length to twice the 3% uncertainty from the squared period, or gives the equivalent fractional calculation.
States a percentage uncertainty in g of 8%.

hints: Convert the percentage uncertainty from the preceding part into a decimal fraction before applying it to the calculated value of g.
Use 8% = 0.08 and multiply it by the value of g found in part (b)(i).
walkthrough: The percentage uncertainty from part (b)(ii) is 8%, which is 0.08 as a decimal fraction.
Use the calculated value from part (b)(i), g = 9.63 m s⁻².
The absolute uncertainty is 0.08 × 9.63 m s⁻² = 0.7704 m s⁻².
To one significant figure, the absolute uncertainty is 0.8 m s⁻².

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the 8% uncertainty as 0.08 of the calculated g value and reports 0.8 m s⁻².
